title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Friuli and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Friuli labels usually name the grape and the DOC, like Collio Friulano or Friuli Colli Orientali Ribolla Gialla. Ramandolo and Colli Orientali del Friuli Picolit are DOCGs for sweet wines. Rosazzo is a small DOCG for white blends. Orange wines may say macerato or skin contact, or be labelled as table wine.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Friulano is traditionally paired with prosciutto di San Daniele, Friuli's famous ham. Crisp whites suit seafood from the Adriatic; orange wines suit richer dishes, mushrooms, pork, aged cheese and spiced food. Refosco suits game and sausages; Picolit suits blue cheese and pastries.

steps.prompt: Which ham is a classic match for Friulano?
steps.explanation: San Daniele is Friuli's own ham.

steps.body: Orange wines' tannin and texture suit food that would overwhelm most whites, like roast pork or mushroom risotto.

steps.prompt: Orange wines are usually served ice cold.
steps.explanation: Not true. They're often served at 12 to 14 degrees, slightly warmer than most whites.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels name the grape and the DOC
Friulano suits San Daniele ham; orange wines suit richer food
